title: Pre-decrement Underflow in Work-Stealing Deque
pattern: Popping an item from the bottom of a work-stealing deque using simple stores and loads without a CAS operation when the deque has only a single element left.
why_bad: When `bottom == top`, there is exactly one element left. A concurrent thief thread could be executing `popTop` and trying to steal that exact element using a CAS on `top`. Without the owner thread also using a CAS on `top` to resolve the conflict, both threads will claim and process the same task.
detection: A work-stealing deque implementation where the local worker pops tasks without using a CAS on `top` when the queue length is 1 or less.
counterexample: The Chase-Lev deque or BoundedDEQueue which switches to a CAS on `top` when `bottom == top`.
